comparison.objective: Candidate commissions a shock absorber through adjustment and repeated impact trials; pr-1300 places a nickel strip and spot-welds it to four battery cells.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate uses a hex key and fine collar rotation with counterholding and retightening. pr-1300 places a thin strip, then positions two welder probes over four terminals and returns the tool.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two non-bottoming, non-overloaded stops with no excessive rebound or setting drift. pr-1300 requires centered strip placement, four 0.2 s dual-probe contacts, tool return, arm retreat, and stillness; its simulated welds do not model bonding.
comparison.reason: Adjustment of a retained damping mechanism and validation through dynamic response tests a different ability from sheet placement and repeated welding-tool contact. Candidate rebound, overload, and drift thresholds remain unspecified.
